summary.interpretation: Codex can call both MCP servers from an isolated config, but current prompting does not reliably produce the desired Kairn-read -> Headroom-compress workflow. The tool-layer matrix is promising; end-to-end agent use needs either stronger instructions or Kairn-native orchestration before public claims.

attempts.interpretation: The agent solved the task and used Kairn MCP, but skipped Headroom because Kairn returned small source/test context. This supports Kairn MCP usefulness, not combo savings.

The agent did call both MCP servers, but compressed Kairn start-task output instead of first reading the exact file payload. This proves both servers can be available to Codex, but not that agents naturally use the optimal combo path.

recommendedNextStep: Implement or prototype a Kairn-side optional compression handoff for large MCP payloads instead of relying on the agent to decide when and how to call Headroom.
